To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CSF samples intended to be used for electron microscopy should be stored at +4 °C for short-term storage.
Borrelia garinnii spirochetes can survive in spiked cerebrospinal fluids (CSF) for at least seven days at +4 °C and can be detected with transmission electron microscopy (TEEM).
Borrelia garini is stable in CSF stored at 4 °C for at least 7 days and is not stable in CSF samples stored at room temperature or frozen.

the optimal conditions for storage of CSF specimens intended for direct diagnosis of neuroborreliosis.
the optimal storage conditions for CSF samples intended either for qPCR or TEM.

CSF samples intended to be analysed by TEM should be stored at +4 °C.

the optimal temperature for short term storage of CSF for direct diagnosis of Borrelia depends on the diagnostic method used.
the optimal storage conditions of CSF samples for direct diagnosis depend on the method of investigation.
the optimal storage conditions should be determined for each material, and for each diagnostic method.
